Numeracy items with their text, for the AI Hub

Source: R/data-ai.R
itemtext.Rd

The text and field-test statistics of 192 simulated Grade 7 numeracy multiple-choice items, written from 12 item models (families) of 16 items each, such as unit rates, percents, elapsed time and simple equations. Within a family the items differ in their numbers, names and contexts, so the data show how far surface features move item difficulty. The items were calibrated with the 2PL on a simulated field test of 1,500 test takers.

Usage

itemtext

Format

A data frame with 192 rows (one per item) and 17 columns: id (N01-01 to N12-16: family and item number), family (the item model), domain (content area), stem (the question), A to D (the options), key (the keyed option), decimal (1 if the item uses decimals or fractions), digits (digits in the largest number), context (1 if the stem starts with a context sentence), a and b (2PL discrimination and difficulty from the field test), a_se and b_se (their standard errors) and p_field (share correct in the field test).

Source

Simulated; the script is data-raw/itemtext.R in the package's GitHub repository.

Details

The dataset is for learning to predict item difficulty from item text and to calibrate item families from automatic item generation. Some problems were planted on purpose; lab_truth("itemtext") lists them and the true item parameters. Some families repeat a stem with different options (for example "Which number is the greatest?"); the extra context sentences are deliberately unrelated to the question, to add reading load.

See also

essays, the other AI Hub dataset; the AI Hub.

Examples

head(itemtext[, c("id", "family", "stem", "key", "b")])
#>       id    family
#> 1 N01-01 Unit rate
#> 2 N01-02 Unit rate
#> 3 N01-03 Unit rate
#> 4 N01-04 Unit rate
#> 5 N01-05 Unit rate
#> 6 N01-06 Unit rate
#>                                                                                                           stem
#> 1                                             A pack of 6 pencils costs $30.00. How much does one pencil cost?
#> 2  Maya is buying supplies for a school trip. A pack of 8 pencils costs $56.00. How much does one pencil cost?
#> 3      Sofia is saving money for a new bike. A pack of 10 pencils costs $30.00. How much does one pencil cost?
#> 4                                             A pack of 5 pencils costs $45.00. How much does one pencil cost?
#> 5                                            A pack of 10 pencils costs $50.00. How much does one pencil cost?
#> 6 Noah is buying supplies for a school trip. A pack of 10 pencils costs $40.00. How much does one pencil cost?
#>   key     b
#> 1   D -0.12
#> 2   A -0.24
#> 3   A -0.35
#> 4   C -0.45
#> 5   D -0.12
#> 6   C -0.32
# family means of difficulty
sort(tapply(itemtext$b, itemtext$family, mean))
#>    Converting units                Mean Area of a rectangle           Unit rate 
#>           -0.744375           -0.689375           -0.555000           -0.145625 
#>       Average speed Percent of a number        Elapsed time         Probability 
#>            0.162500            0.337500            0.389375            0.458750 
#>               Ratio    Adding fractions  Comparing decimals   Solving equations 
#>            0.620000            0.872500            1.110625            1.149375 
# surface features and difficulty
summary(lm(b ~ family + decimal + digits + context, data = itemtext))
